title: US judge extends media outlets' White House access
summary: A federal judge extended the order that blocks the Trump administration from banning three media outlets from the White House. The outlets have reasonable grounds to think they'll win the case, the…

image.caption: The Trump administration banned three outlets from entering the WHite HouseImage: Aaron Schwartz/CNP/ZUMA/IMAGO

blocks.text: A US federal judge has extended the order to allow three US media outlets to report from the White House, despite the Trump administration trying to ban them.
The three outlets, CNN, MS NOW and Politico, filed a lawsuit against the decision due to constitutional free speech and due process claims.
In September, District Judge Timothy Kelly issued an order to temporarily restore the journalists' access to the White House.

On Tuesday, Judge Kelly rulled that President Donald Trump likely broke the law by trying to ban them. He then issued a preliminary injunction to extend this previous order for the duration of the case.

The judge — who was nominated by Trump — added that the decision should not be interpreted as "claiming that President Donald Trump's claims about accuracy and fairness in the media's reporting are unfounded."
